Its government-in-exile continues to operate from a host country (State M), but its population is dispersed globally, with most acquiring temporary protection status. When State M decides to deport these individuals, citing national security, a group files a complaint before the Human Rights Committee under the ICCPR, claiming that forced return would violate their right to life and family under international human rights law. State M argues that environmental migrants are not protected under the 1951 Refugee Convention but are protected under customary international law and that they can go to other third countries. Can State K’s displaced citizens claim protection against deportation based on international law?
